title: National Gallery Prague: Masterpieces
subtitle: Twenty works from the National Gallery Prague, moving between self-portrait, allegory and inhabited landscape.
introduction:
In one self-portrait, Henri Rousseau makes himself much larger than the city behind him. In another, Pepa Mařáková places herself beside her father and their painting equipment. Both announce an artist's presence, but they give that presence a different setting: a public landscape in one case, a shared working relationship in the other.

The National Gallery Prague selection moves between such individual identities and figures asked to represent something larger, including Slavia, charity and a regional community. Landscapes also contain human choices, whether in cultivated plots or sharply reorganised colour. The entries follow these changes without proposing that all twenty works belong to one style or one national story.
visitNote: National Gallery Prague occupies several buildings. This focused collection selection is not a walking route or a complete list of its principal holdings. Works can move between displays or leave on loan; consult the gallery’s current location information before travelling.

books.title: Concerning the Spiritual in Art
books.author: Wassily Kandinsky; translated by Michael Sadleir
books.note: Kandinsky’s writing supplies one contemporary argument for colour becoming independent of literal description. Compare it with Špála’s pink landscapes and angular bodies without assuming that the paintings illustrate the book’s ideas.

works.title: Josephine Crane-Bradley as Slavia
works.catalogueTitle: Portrait of Josephine Crane-Bradley as Slavia
works.credit: Alphonse Mucha. Portrait of Josephine Crane-Bradley as Slavia. Image credit: Alphonse Mucha; Source credit: Národní galerie v Praze. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: The seated woman remains a particular sitter, but her ceremonial dress and emblematic surroundings ask her to represent Slavia as well. Portrait and personification therefore coexist rather than replacing one another. The patterned frame helps make that transformation public: a named individual is presented within a design whose meaning extends beyond her biography.

works.title: Czech Heart
works.credit: Alphonse Mucha. Czech Heart. Image credit: Alphonse Mucha; Source credit: National Gallery Prague. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Proportional resize and JPEG compression; full source frame retained.
works.description: The woman's lowered hand and the child's slight body make an unequal relation of care immediately legible. Mucha reduces the allegorical task to a close encounter instead of multiplying decorative signs. The title asks for a larger meaning, but the physical relation between these two figures supplies its clearest foundation.

works.title: Self-Portrait from Île Saint-Louis
works.catalogueTitle: Self Portrait from L'ile Saint Louis
works.credit: Henri Rousseau. Self Portrait from L'ile Saint Louis. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: Palette and brush identify the large dark figure as a painter, while the city behind provides a world in which he claims a place. The museum calls the work *Myself: Portrait–Landscape*, a useful description of its unequal partnership. The surroundings remain recognisable without controlling the scale of the artist standing before them.

works.title: Tatyana Repina, the Artist’s Mother
works.credit: Ilya Repin. Tatyana Repina, the Artist's Mother. WikiArt source label: Public domain. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/ilya-repin/tatyana-repina-the-artist-s-mother-1867
works.description: The shawl encloses the face, and the close crop removes hands and most of the body from consideration. Repin's mother is consequently presented through a limited set of features and fabric. The family relationship supplies context, but it does not authorise a story about her thoughts at the moment represented.

works.title: The Gardens of l’Hermitage, Pontoise
works.credit: The Gardens of l'Hermitage, Pontoise. WikiArt; Camille Pissarro. Proportional resizing and JPEG compression; source frame preserved.
works.description: The hillside is cultivated rather than untouched. Walls, paths and planted plots divide it before the small workers become distinct, so human activity is visible in the land's structure as well as in its inhabitants. Pissarro gives gardening and settlement a scale that remains legible across a view dominated by trees, houses and sky.

works.title: Nocturne
works.credit: Robert Macaulay Stevenson. Nocturne. Image credit: Robert Macaulay Stevenson; Source credit: National Gallery in Prague. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: Trees and their reflections establish matching dark shapes around the water. A small bright area becomes conspicuous within the restricted tonal range. Since the available reproduction is monochrome, colour cannot safely carry the explanation; the important relations visible here are between silhouettes, light intervals and the darker areas enclosing them.

works.title: A Road on Lopud
works.credit: Václav Špála. A Road on Lopud. Image credit: Václav Špála; Source credit: https://sbirky.ngprague.cz/dielo/CZE:NG.O_8598. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: The road remains a route through the landscape, but angular trees and planes of pink, blue and green prevent it from opening as one continuous corridor. Špála gives forward movement a series of visual interruptions. Recognisable geography and conspicuous colour construction coexist, neither entirely subordinated to the other.

works.title: Eve with an Apple
works.credit: Václav Špála. Eve with an Apple. Image credit: Václav Špála; Source credit: https://sbirky.ngprague.cz/en/dielo/CZE:NG.O_7979. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: The large red-pink body is held by dark outlines against green slopes and blue sky. Its scale gives Eve a presence comparable to the terrain around her. The broad areas of colour join figure and landscape on the painted surface, while their distinct boundaries keep the subject readable.

works.title: Self-Portrait
works.credit: Václav Špála. Self-Portrait. Image credit: Václav Špála; Source credit: https://sbirky.ngprague.cz/en/dielo/CZE:NG.O_3482. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: The palette announces the sitter's occupation; the blue and green divisions across his face demonstrate what that occupation can involve. Likeness does not require every patch to imitate a conventional skin tone. In this self-portrait, the painter's identity is carried by the handling of colour as well as by the tools shown across his lap.

works.title: Three Washerwomen
works.credit: Václav Špála. Three Washerwomen. Image credit: Václav Špála; Source credit: https://sbirky.ngprague.cz/en/dielo/CZE:NG.O_9019. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: The washerwomen are difficult to separate because bent backs and arms fit into a shared pattern of angles. Their repeated labour supplies the basis for that pattern. The picture reduces the surrounding setting, leaving the act of washing recognisable through the positions it requires rather than through an inventory of domestic objects.

works.title: At an Exhibition in Paris
works.credit: Karel Špillar. At an Exhibition in Paris. Image credit: Karel Špillar; National Gallery Prague. https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Karel_%C5%A0pillar_-_At_an_Exhibition_in_Paris_-_O_6492_-_National_Gallery_Prague.jpg. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Full-frame resize and JPEG compression; applicable ShareAlike terms retained.
works.description: An exhibition normally directs attention toward its artworks. Špillar directs it instead toward the people walking, standing and looking among them. The foreground figure establishes a near position within this social space, while pictures and display stands become its setting. Visiting art is itself made into an activity worth depicting.

works.title: In a Café
works.credit: Karel Špillar. In a Café. Image credit: Karel Špillar; National Gallery Prague. https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Karel_%C5%A0pillar_-_In_a_Caf%C3%A9_-_O_5283_-_National_Gallery_Prague.jpg. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Full-frame resize and JPEG compression; applicable ShareAlike terms retained.
works.description: Hats, flowers and cups give the café a social character even where faces remain partly withheld. Light clothing loosens into the warmer surrounding marks, making the people less separate from the room. The picture offers shared occupation of a public place without supplying a definite conversation for the figures at its table.

works.title: Children Receiving Breakfast
works.credit: Ferdinand Georg Waldmüller. Children received their breakfast. Image credit: Ferdinand Georg Waldmüller; Source credit: repro from artbook. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: The doorway divides the bright exterior from the dark room, placing the children at different points of visibility. Food passes among them while the boy by the outer wall stands more clearly apart. A shared breakfast contains distinct positions of waiting and receiving; the group need not be treated as one uniform expression of childhood.

works.title: Count and Countess von Hartig as Roman Charity
works.catalogueTitle: Count Franz de Paula Graf von Hartig and his wife Eleanore as Caritas Romana
works.credit: Barbara Krafft. Count Franz de Paula Graf von Hartig and his wife Eleanore as Caritas Romana. Image credit: Barbara Krafft; Source credit: kultura.zpravy.idnes.cz. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: Named sitters take on the subject of Roman Charity, so the picture asks to be understood as both a double portrait and a borrowed story. Their close bodily arrangement would be unusual in a straightforward social likeness. The historical role affects how they are presented without making the painted incident an event from their own lives.

works.title: Diogenes
works.credit: Maximilian Pirner. Diogenes. Image credit: Maximilian Pirner; National Gallery Prague. https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Max_Pirner_-_Diogenes_-_O_5069_-_National_Gallery_Prague.jpg. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Full-frame resize and JPEG compression; applicable ShareAlike terms retained.
works.description: The elderly philosopher bends near his barrel while airborne figures occupy a different register above. Rough ground and simple shelter give the lower figure a tangible place, against which the upper fantasy can be measured. The picture's two zones remain connected through their contrast in bodily need, position and apparent freedom of movement.

works.title: Evening Silence
works.credit: Antonín Hudeček. Evening Silence. Image credit: Antonín Hudeček; National Gallery Prague. https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Anton%C3%ADn_Hude%C4%8Dek_-_Evening_Silence_-_O_8411_-_National_Gallery_Prague.jpg. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Full-frame resize and JPEG compression; applicable ShareAlike terms retained.
works.description: The woman faces the valley, leaving her expression unavailable. Her position gives the landscape someone within it who also looks outward, while the curved path keeps the foreground connected to distance. The dusk can hold attention without a narrated event. Stillness is established through the arrangement, not through a claim about what she feels.

works.title: Self-Portrait with Her Father
works.credit: Pepa Mařáková. Self-Portrait with Her Father. Image credit: Pepa Mařáková; National Gallery Prague. https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Pepa_Ma%C5%99%C3%A1kov%C3%A1_-_Self-Portrait_with_Her_Father_-_O_3591_-_National_Gallery_Prague.jpg. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Full-frame resize and JPEG compression; applicable ShareAlike terms retained.
works.description: Mařáková faces outward while her father turns toward her, allowing the two directions of attention to remain unequal. Their painting equipment makes this a shared professional setting as well as a family portrait. Her father taught her and enabled informal access to the Prague Academy at a time when women could not enroll: the relationship had practical consequences beyond this room.

works.title: Mountain Lake in the Giant Mountains
works.catalogueTitle: Mountain Lake in the Giant Mountains
works.credit: Otakar Lebeda. Mountain Lake in the Giant Mountains. Image credit: Otakar Lebeda; Source credit: National Gallery in Prague. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: The lake lies low within steep surrounding slopes, giving the mountains an enclosing structure. Broken foreground rocks establish a nearer, rougher scale before the eye reaches the water. Rather than opening into an unlimited panorama, the landscape measures distance through the terrain that contains it.

works.title: Moravian Slovak Madonna: Moravian Song
works.credit: Joža Uprka. Moravian Slovak Madonna (Moravian Song). Image credit: Joža Uprka; National Gallery Prague. https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Jo%C5%BEa_Uprka_-_Moravian_Slovak_Madonna_(Moravian_Song)_-_O_3919_-_National_Gallery_Prague.jpg. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Full-frame resize and JPEG compression; applicable ShareAlike terms retained.
works.description: The central devotional figure and the people in regional dress operate at different scales of attention. Three panels provide room for a shared religious focus and many participants in communal ceremony. Clothing and repeated gestures give the gathering local specificity, keeping the triptych from functioning as an interchangeable image of worship.

works.title: Sunday on the Periphery
works.credit: Georges Kars. Sunday on the Periphery. Image credit: Georges Kars; National Gallery Prague. https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Ji%C5%99%C3%AD_Kars_-_Sunday_on_the_Periphery_-_O_12797_-_National_Gallery_Prague.jpg. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Full-frame resize and JPEG compression; applicable ShareAlike terms retained.
works.description: Resting figures and people in motion share the angular forms of the trees and ground. The public landscape is compressed rather than divided neatly into isolated bodies and a distant backdrop. Sunday leisure is thus presented through a common pictorial structure, even though the people within it remain occupied in different ways.

closingSections.title: Compare roles, then dates
paragraphs: Place Rousseau, Mařáková and Špála together in Artline to compare how each pictures the work of being an artist. Their dates provide context, not proof of a direct relationship. The National Gallery uses several buildings and changing displays; check the relevant collection and work before choosing a visiting route.
